36		Repo    string // forge repo name

53	// found, returns what can be known offline about the mirror this clone points
54	// at. `origin` is preferred; otherwise remotes are considered in name order so
55	// the reported remote is stable across runs. Returns nil when no remote points
56	// at a mirror (the common case for an ordinary clone).
57	func detectMirrorClone(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string) *mirrorClone {
58		for _, name := range orderedRemoteNames(ctx, repoRoot) {
59			rawURL, gerr := gitremote.GetRemoteURLInDir(ctx, repoRoot, name)
60			if gerr != nil {
61				continue
62			}
63			info, perr := gitremote.ParseURL(rawURL)
64			if perr != nil || info.Protocol != gitremote.ProtocolEntire {
65				continue
66			}
67			return &mirrorClone{
68				Remote:  name,
69				Cluster: info.Host,
70				Owner:   info.Owner,
71				Repo:    info.Repo,
72				URL:     rawURL,
73			}
74		}

79	// (e.g. "github.com") when that host is one Entire can mirror — the case where
80	// pointing the clone at a mirror is a meaningful next step. ok is false when no
81	// remote names a mirrorable forge (an already-mirrored entire:// remote, or a
82	// host mirrors don't support). The host is read straight from the remote URL so
83	// the hint names the real provider rather than a hardcoded one, and gating on
84	// gitremote.IsSupportedForge means the trigger widens automatically if more
85	// forges become mirrorable. This is a purely local check: it cannot tell

93				continue
94			}

101			}

108	// origin-preferring result. Returns nil on any error (treated as "no remotes").
109	func orderedRemoteNames(ctx context.Context, repoRoot string) []string {
110		remotes, err := gitremote.ListRemotesInDir(ctx, repoRoot)
111		if err != nil || len(remotes) == 0 {
112			return nil
113		}

115		rest := make([]string, 0, len(remotes))
116		for _, name := range remotes {

119				continue
120			}

122		}
